discovery: Invention of quantum key distribution: cryptographic security founded on the laws of quantum physics

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

subfield: Quantum optics and quantum information (quantum communication)
motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84, 1984) showed that the no-cloning principle and measurement disturbance of single quanta make eavesdropping detectable, so a secret key can be distributed with security guaranteed by physics rather than by computational assumptions. Ekert (1991) independently linked key security to entanglement and violation of Bell inequalities, turning a foundational test of nonlocality into a cryptographic resource and seeding device-independent security and certified randomness. Their ideas transformed quantum mechanics from a theory of puzzles into an engineering discipline: QKD has since been realised over metropolitan fibre networks, in daylight free-space links, and between ground stations and orbiting satellites, establishing the field of quantum communication and the emerging quantum internet. Few theoretical inventions in physics have opened so many new experimental frontiers and practical technologies, while deepening our understanding of information, measurement and entanglement.
